newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Company threatens to cut power on Marcos crypt.
newsitem.headline: Company threatens to cut power on Marcos crypt.

text.p: A Philippine power distributor threatened on Friday to pull the plug on the mausoleum of the late President Ferdinand Marcos after his family allegedly failed to pay the bills.

The Ilocos Norte Electric Cooperative will cut power supply on March 3 to the mausoleum, where Marcos' preserved corpse has lain since 1993 lit by soft lights 24 hours a day, after his family failed to settle 5.643 million pesos ($214,500) of bills by Friday, an official of the cooperative said.
"We have given them (the Marcos family) enough time to pay their bills," the cooperative's general manager Romillas Pascual told Reuters.
Former First Lady Imelda Marcos, now a congresswoman, was not immediately available for comment. An aide told Reuters she was "out of town".

Pascual said the cooperative will also cut power to the Marcos mansion and a museum housing his memorabilia, both located in the same compound as the mausoleum holding the former president's corpse encased in an elevated glass coffin in the Marcos hometown of Batac in the northern Philippines.

Power to the Marcos mansion was interrupted in April last year after the family failed to settle accumulated bills after they left for exile in Hawaii in 1986, but it was restored several days later after a son-in-law made a partial payment.

The cooperative at that time spared the mausoleum in deference to the town's "favourite son," after local government officials asked the cooperative to give the family enough time to settle the bills.
The Marcoses were overthrown in a 1986 popular revolt after being accused of stealing up to $5 billion from the country's coffers. Marcos died in Hawaii three years later.
In 1992, his family brought his remains to his home province but refused to bury him, saying he deserved to be buried in the capital, Manila.
The government denied the request, fearing it could provoke unrest among diehard Marcos "loyalists".
